reason: The meal's glucose-rich blood is linked to the same body, so I’ll begin by bringing the two together.

effect: The body now shows the post-meal rise in blood glucose; pancreatic sensing is the next likely step.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells can detect the rising glucose and begin the response.
expectation: The pancreatic cells will respond to elevated blood glucose, likely by releasing insulin.

effect: The pancreatic beta cells released insulin into blood, with routes toward muscle and liver.
reason: The insulin route points toward muscle, which is available to show a response.
expectation: Muscle will respond to insulin by taking up more glucose from the blood.

effect: Muscle takes up glucose in response to insulin, and the new goal shifts attention to maintaining blood glucose between meals.
reaction: The feedback showing less insulin as glucose falls was useful.
reason: Advancing time should establish the between-meal conditions before the liver responds.

choice.combine: Body taking up glucose into muscle

expectation: Blood glucose will fall as tissues keep using it and incoming glucose tapers.

effect: Blood glucose has fallen between meals while liver glycogen remains available.
reaction: The time shift made the next problem clear.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells may detect falling glucose and initiate the between-meal response.
expectation: Pancreatic alpha cells will release glucagon into the blood.

alternatives.reason: The liver could directly show how stored glycogen supplies glucose.

effect: The pancreatic alpha cells released glucagon into the blood, with its route leading toward the liver.
reaction: That matched the expected between-meal response.
reason: The liver contains glycogen and is the indicated target of the glucagon signal.
expectation: The liver will break down glycogen and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose from glycogen, and rising blood glucose reduced glucagon release, completing the between-meal feedback sequence.
reaction: The sequential insets made the feedback response clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: The paired insulin and glucagon responses were most worthwhile: they connected changing blood glucose to different pancreatic signals and tissue responses, with feedback as glucose changed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding glucose-rich blood to the body was straightforward setup, but its result added little beyond the initial picture.

surprise.text: The later inset showed insulin release decreasing as muscle uptake reduced blood glucose, making feedback visible rather than ending at hormone action.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the pancreas and liver were clearly indicated by the changing conditions and signal routes.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: following the same body through opposing responses and seeing feedback in the planned illustrations made the system connections interesting. The sequence was predictable, though, so I would hope for more meaningful choices.
